subject: Availability standby: quick update and action items
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Availability standby: quick update and action items

Carlos —

Quick note while the ops team continues to monitor: we saw a short-lived spike in tail latencies for models in your region between 08:42–08:55 PT. The runtime team applied a targeted kernel fallback which reduced error rates and restored normal throughput. We are keeping a close watch on the cluster and have a small on-call posture in case of recurrence.

What this means for Aurora Tech: there is no data loss and no config change on your side. We recommend the following small actions to minimize impact if we see another spike:

- (Action) If you have long-running streaming sessions, consider retry-on-5xx with jitter for 10s before escalating.
- (Action) Reduce max tokens for non-critical generation jobs for the next 12 hours.
- (Optional) If you want, we can route your critical routes to Reserved capacity for the next 24 hours (we can activate burst capacity).

Attached is a snapshot of latency by model shard and a short checklist with who to call.

We will send an executive summary at close-of-day and a follow-up with root-cause analysis once available. If you want an earlier sync, Ben (copied) can hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0102

Attachments: latency-snapshot-1029.png, standby-action-items-1029.pdf
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@aurora-tech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:25:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability standby: quick update and action items

Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up and for the quick mitigation. We did see a handful of 500s on our side for a small subset of high-throughput endpoints (orders stream). No customer-facing outages yet, but support has a couple of tickets.

A couple of asks:
- Can you confirm whether KV-cache warming could have been affected? We rely on prefix caching for a few bulk jobs.
- If we take Reserved capacity for the next 24 hrs, what's the lead time to enable?

If it's helpful, I can open a brief bridge for engineers — ops@aurora-tech.ai is standing by.

—Carlos
Head of Platform | Aurora Tech
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability standby: quick update and action items

Internal note —

Summary of what happened so far:
- 08:42–08:55 PT: tail latency spike on two shards serving gpt-4-like open-model; increased 5xxs on streaming endpoints.
- 08:56 PT: runtime applied kernel fallback and drained hot queues; error rate dropped to baseline by ~09:02 PT.
- No configuration changes were rolled to customer routes.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- [Ben] Continue sampling logs for memory pressure; follow up by 11:00 PT with any correlation to recent quantization changes.
- [Stephanie] Confirm whether prefix/KV cache misses spiked for Aurora's route; reach out to ingester team if so.
- [Jonas] Prepare a short canary plan to route Aurora critical routes to dedicated pool if we see a second spike.

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Availability standby: quick update and action items

Carlos —

Follow-up at close-of-day with the actions we committed to earlier today. Short executive summary below and next steps.

Executive summary:
- Impact: short-lived tail latency spike (08:42–08:55 PT) increased 5xxs for a narrow subset of streaming endpoints. No customer data loss, no long-term outage.
- Mitigation: runtime fallback reduced error rate to baseline by ~09:02 PT.
- Status: stable. We have a heightened watch and a small on-call posture through 02:00 PT tomorrow.

Immediate actions we completed:
- We verified KV cache hit-rate for Aurora routes — Stephanie: cache miss rate rose ~3.1% during the spike, but recovered quickly. No cache corruption found.
- Ben instrumented additional telemetry for memory pressure and is running a retention check on the affected worker pool.
- Jonas prepared a canary plan to temporarily shift critical traffic into Dedicated capacity if we observe a recurrence; lead time for enabling burst reserved is ~20 minutes once you approve.

Recommended customer actions (for your ops team):
- Apply retry-on-5xx with exponential backoff for long-running streams for the next 12 hours.
- If you'd like Reserved capacity for the next 24 hours, reply with approval and we will trigger the canary and provide a passphrase for traffic routing.

Attachments: standby-action-items-1029.pdf (contains the canary play and on-call contact list).

We will follow up with a formal postmortem draft within 48 hours that will include root cause analysis and a timeline. If you'd like a bridge now, we can spin one up — otherwise we'll proceed with monitoring and the postmortem.

Thanks for your partnership — appreciate the quick coordination.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
